_comment: br-frankenpandas-sabdt. ONE fixture, named explicitly, because bulk
regeneration is forbidden and this pin is load-bearing evidence.
fp_p2d_017_column_dtype_check_int_only_hardened pins expected_dtype
'int64' for the payload [int64 1, null, int64 3]. MEASURED, live pandas
2.2.3: NO construction of that payload yields 'int64'. The oracle's own
chooser (series_dtype_for_payload_values maps {int64}+null -> 'Int64')
gives the NULLABLE extension 'Int64'; plain inference gives 'float64'.
The pinned value is reachable from neither, so it is stale rather than a
decision anyone made.
This re-bank makes the corpus assert MORE of the extension behaviour, not
less. It is the opposite of the forbidden regenerate-to-float64 move that
DISC-011 warns against, and the opposite of regenerating to force green:
the fixture is green TODAY only because the harness builds a plain
DType::Int64 whose name() coincidentally matches the stale pin, and it
goes RED the moment the br-frankenpandas-vprpg payload-dtype chooser
lands. Re-banking it is a precondition for that chooser, not a way to
avoid its consequences.
The assertion was UNVERIFIABLE until br-frankenpandas-62d1s (7ebf937c1)
implemented the oracle's column_dtype_check op — before that the oracle
could not run the operation at all, which is how a pin nothing produced
survived in the corpus.

fp_p2d_017_column_dtype_check_int_only_h.evidence: live pandas 2.2.3: pd.Series([1, None, 3], dtype='Int64').dtype -> Int64; pd.Series([1, None, 3]).dtype -> float64; neither is int64
